title: Avocado Fat: How Much It Has, What Type, and How It Compares

seo.title: Avocado Fat: Amount and Type
seo.meta_description: Avocado provides about 14.7 g fat per 100 g, mostly monounsaturated. Compare it with olive oil, nuts, butter and other fruit.
seo.search_intent: Understand the amount and type of fat in avocado.

excerpt: Avocado contains about 14.7 g fat per 100 g: roughly 9.8 g monounsaturated, 1.8 g polyunsaturated and 2.1 g saturated. Oleic acid is the dominant fatty acid.
content_html:
Avocado is unusual among fruit because much of its energy comes from fat. Per 100 g it provides about 14.7 g fat and 160 calories. Most of that fat is monounsaturated, with oleic acid as the dominant fatty acid.

Fat breakdown

Per 100 g avocadoApprox. amount
Total fat14.7 g
Monounsaturated fat~9.8 g
Polyunsaturated fat~1.8 g
Saturated fat~2.1 g
Calories160
Fiber6.7 g

About two-thirds of avocado fat is monounsaturated. Saturated fat is a much smaller share, around 2.1 g out of 14.7 g total.

Oleic acid

Oleic acid is the major monounsaturated fat in both avocado and olive oil. Public-health guidance favors replacing some saturated fats with unsaturated fats.

Unsaturated fat still provides energy: all dietary fat supplies about 9 calories per gram.

Avocado vs butter

Avocado contains around 2.1 g saturated fat/100 g, while butter contains more than 50 g/100 g. Equal weights therefore differ by more than twentyfold in saturated fat.

A practical toast comparison is more useful: 10 g butter provides about 5 g saturated fat and 72 calories; 50 g avocado provides about 1 g saturated fat and 80 calories plus roughly 3.4 g fiber.

Avocado vs olive oil

Olive oil is essentially pure fat: about 100 g fat and 884 calories/100 g. Avocado has 14.7 g fat and 160 calories because roughly three-quarters of its weight is water.

One tablespoon of oil in the U.S. is about 14 g and roughly 120 calories; 50 g avocado is about 80 calories. Avocado adds fiber and volume, while oil delivers much more fat in a smaller amount.

Avocado vs nuts

Almonds are around 50 g fat and 579 calories/100 g; walnuts around 65 g and 654 calories. Avocado at 14.7 g and 160 calories is far less concentrated because it contains much more water.

Is it a “healthy fat”?

The phrase is useful when it refers to a fat profile dominated by unsaturated fats, particularly when those foods replace sources rich in saturated fat. WHO guidance favors unsaturated over saturated fat.

Replacement matters. Swapping butter for avocado changes fat quality; adding avocado without replacing anything raises the meal's total energy.

The whole food

Avocado also provides about 6.7 g fiber and roughly 485 mg potassium per 100 g. Olive oil contains no fiber, illustrating why two foods rich in oleic acid are not nutritionally identical.

Portion sizes

Avocado fleshCaloriesFat
50 g807.3 g
100 g16014.7 g
150 g24022 g

Avocados vary widely in size, so grams are more reliable than assuming “half an avocado” is always the same portion.

Bottom line

Avocado fat is mostly monounsaturated. It is high-fat compared with apples or oranges, but much lower in fat concentration than nuts or oil. Its nutritional profile combines unsaturated fat with fiber, potassium and the water-rich matrix of a whole fruit.

Sources

Composition comes from USDA FoodData Central. Fat-quality guidance comes from the World Health Organization.

faq.question: How much fat is in avocado?
faq.answer: About 14.7 g/100 g, including roughly 9.8 g monounsaturated and 2.1 g saturated fat.

faq.question: Does avocado have more fat than nuts?
faq.answer: No. Almonds are around 50 g fat/100 g and walnuts around 65 g, versus 14.7 g in avocado.

faq.question: Is avocado fat the same as olive oil?
faq.answer: Both are rich in oleic acid, but olive oil is almost pure fat and about 884 calories/100 g versus 160 for avocado.
